reason: Narrower. In Bromeliaceae and similar groups, primary bracts are the bracts that subtend the branches of the inflorescence, as opposed to floral bracts. That is exactly PO's definition of inflorescence bract ('a bract subtending a branch of the inflorescence').

Narrower. Most uses count them per side ('5-7 primary nerves on each side'), so they are the first-order lateral veins. This follows the earlier rules primary lateral vein and lateral nerve → PO_0020140. Some French uses in the singular ('nervure primaire très proéminente') mean the midrib, PO_0020139; a rule keyed on the plural or 'on each side' would avoid that.

Narrower. A clump is a tuft of shoots of one plant or of a clonal colony, and PO lists 'woody clump' and 'clonal colony' as synonyms of whole plant. Its size and density inhere in the plant. 'In clumps' as a habit is better expressed by the caespitose phenotype, FLOPO_0985036.

Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. Floras use it for the mouth of the perigynium beak, of the leaf sheath (Carex), of the corolla, and so on. Same reason as the earlier rejections of mouth-like words (throat, opening).

Narrower. The sarcotesta is the fleshy outer layer of the testa (cycads, Ginkgo, Punica, Magnoliaceae). PO has testa and exotesta (only the epidermis) but no sarcotesta. The fleshiness can be annotated as a quality, so a rule is better than a new term.

target: bract apex (PO_0025154) part of involucral bract (PO_0009045)
reason: Phyllary is a narrow synonym of involucral bract (earlier rule C250). Its apex is the region 'apex' of that class, and PO has bract apex.

Narrower. An umbellet is a partial umbel of a compound umbel (PO_0030129 / PO_0030130), i.e. a sub-inflorescence arising from the main inflorescence axis, which is how PO defines second order inflorescence.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of the middle region of the leaf lamina (PO_0020039)
reason: In moss floras these are the lamina cells at mid-leaf: cells of a qualified whole (pattern 12). The region 'middle' is not yet among the region context words. PO_0008020 'central zone of the leaf lamina' is a possible whole. Leaf terms in PO also cover phyllids.

Ambiguous. In FNA it is mostly the involucral fruit husk of Carya and Juglandaceae ('husk winged to base', 'sutures winged'). PO's synonym husk → inflorescence bract (PO_0009054) fits the maize husk, not that one. Other uses refer to any outer fruit covering.

label: stamen fascicle
parent: is_a collective plant organ structure (PO_0025007); part_of androecium (PO_0009061)
definition: A collective plant organ structure (PO:0025007) that is part of an androecium (PO:0009061) and consists of a group of stamens (PO:0009029) whose filaments are connate at least at the base, as in Malvaceae, Hypericaceae and Myrtaceae.
reason: A real structure found in six floras. Counts of stamen fascicles ('5, 10 or 15 phalanges') are a standard character and cannot be expressed with stamen or androecium. PO has no class for it. Propose it to PO upstream.
Narrower. A gland placed between the stamens. It follows the earlier rule gland → PO_0005656. Disc gland (FLOPO_0986045) is too specific, because not all interstaminal glands belong to a disc.
A density unit ('10-15 lateral veins per cm'), not a structure. Like 'per node' and 'per side' in the earlier review.
The second term of a length ratio ('1/2-3/4 the length of the calyx'). This is pattern 10, ratio to another part, with calyx PO_0009060 as the reference. Like 'leaf length' and 'times calyx' earlier.
Exact in usage: a sub-inflorescence of the whole inflorescence. Counts ('with 3-5 partial inflorescences') map to PO's second order inflorescence.

Two unrelated structures share the name. In Acanthaceae it is the hooked funicle (jaculator) that throws the seeds ('long and curved', 'subacute at tip'). In Apocynaceae and orchids it is the corpusculum or viscid gland of the pollinarium ('ellipsoid', 'linear-oblong'). It cannot be grounded without the family.
A surface marking, not a structure. Its presence and number are the quality striated (PATO_0001410) of the part that bears the striae, which is counted with pattern 3 ('4-5-striate').

Narrower. A raceme-like inflorescence whose units are cymules or fascicles. It is not a PO raceme (PO_0030115), so mapping it there would be wrong. Grounding to inflorescence loses the type; a FLOPO inflorescence-type value could be considered later.

A quality (PATO_0000454 hairy), here produced by a lemmatisation error on the noun hairs/poils. The noun should ground to trichome (PO_0000282), which lists hair as a synonym. A bearer rule on 'hairy' would misfire on its adjectival uses.
A fragment of relative measurements ('1/3-1/2 as long as spikelet'), handled by pattern 10, ratio to another part.

target: corolla lobe (FLOPO_0986006) part of corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017), lower
reason: A lobe of a qualified whole (pattern 12). It follows the earlier rule corolla lower lip → corolla lip (C398), with the lip qualified as lower.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to (cell wall, ovary wall, fruit wall, capsule wall). Like 'layer' and 'membrane' earlier.

label: stipule scar
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of shoot axis (PO_0025029)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) that is the mark left on a shoot axis (PO:0025029) where a stipule (PO:0020041) has been shed.
reason: A real structure and a common diagnostic character (Magnoliaceae, Moraceae, Rubiaceae), with its own qualities: annular, fringed, pubescent. It is a sibling of leaf scar (FLOPO_0986052). Propose it to PO upstream together with leaf scar.

target: plant cell (PO_0009002) part of leaf base (PO_0020040)
reason: Cells of a qualified whole (pattern 12). PO's leaf base covers both vascular and non-vascular leaves (the moss usage here).
A colour or surface marking, not a structure: the quality striated (PATO_0001410) or a colour pattern of the part that bears the stripes. Counts go by pattern 3 ('7-16-striate').
The quality striated (PATO_0001410) of the part that bears the striations. Counts go by pattern 3.

Narrower. The claw is the narrowed, stalk-like basal part of a petal. The shape itself is the quality clawed (FLOPO_0991169), so a separate class is not needed. Plain 'claw' stays rejected as generic.
A count of one ('stems single', 'flowers single'), a value of the amount of the part named next to it.

target: region of spadix inflorescence (PO_0030120) or spike inflorescence (PO_0030117) bearing the pistillate flowers; qualifier female (PATO_0000383) via context word 'pistillate'
reason: The female flower-bearing zone of a spadix (Araceae) or spike (Typha), i.e. a region of an existing inflorescence class. If several floras need the zones as bearers, they could become siblings of spadix appendix (FLOPO_0986049) later.

Narrower. In mosses it is the gametophore (PO_0030018, is_a shoot system), from widths of 0.3-1.3 mm. In vascular plants (bamboos, 'leafy shoots 2-5 m tall') it is a vegetative shoot system. The common parent covers both senses.
A colour marking, not a structure: the quality blotchy (PATO_0000329) of the petal or lip that bears it. Its colour and shape are better recorded as attributes of the marking than as a bearer.
